## Licensing overhaul — Phase 3 batch

This release ships the first batch of the ground-up licensing overhaul
locked in v10.36. Customer-side changes only; vendor portal split into
private creator + public verifier lands in a later release.

### What's new

**Support plan semver gate on updates** — minor and major version bumps
now require an active support plan. Patches and rollbacks remain
available regardless of SUP status. Customers see a renewal CTA on the
Updates page when their SUP is lapsed and a minor/major release is
out. Enforced in two layers: the Updates page filter excludes blocked
versions from the catalog, and the install endpoints return HTTP 403
with a structured `sup_required_for_version` body so a hand-rolled
POST still gets gated.

**Lapsed-SUP customers can add cameras within cap** — previously,
lapsed support blocked adding new cameras. Now the device cap is the
gate, not the SUP date. Perpetual licenses stay perpetual.

**Expired demo hard cutoff** — when a demo license's `expires_at`
passes, ingest workers stop processing camera events, the portal goes
read-only (35 mutation endpoints return HTTP 423 Locked), and all
camera configs are preserved. Installing a paid license immediately
resumes operation. No data is destroyed; no migration is needed.

**Dead-state license auto-purge** — rows that have been in a dead
band (wrong_system_id, expired, revoked, invalid_signature) for more
than 30 days are automatically soft-removed by a new cleanup worker
running every 6 hours. Each purge fires an `license_auto_purged`
audit log entry.

### New endpoints

* `GET /api/v1/system/license-block-status` — read-only view of the
  derived block flags (`blocks_ingest`, `blocks_writes`,
  `blocks_add_seat`). Used by the upcoming portal banner UI; available
  to any signed-in user.

### Schema

* `licenses.state_first_observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ` — new column. Stamped
  when a row enters a dead band; cleared on recovery. Drives the
  30-day cleanup grace period. Idempotent ALTER on first boot, no
  downtime.

### Internal architecture

* New `system_config[license_block_status]` JSON row published by the
  api's licensing reverify cycle. Worker containers (db-writer,
  ftp-ingest) poll this row every 60s instead of re-running the
  signature verify pipeline themselves. Fail-open if the row is
  missing or the api is down.

### Test surface

* api: 343 → 401 tests
* db-writer: 13 → 22 tests
* ftp-ingest: 7 → 15 tests

# v0.1.30 — Offline Activation Handshake

This release adds a tidy two-step flow for customers on closed or
air-gapped networks to request a license, expansion, SUP renewal,
or re-issue without copy/pasting your system_id by hand.

## What's new

**Download system info — Licensing page**

A new **Download system info** button appears at the top of the
System → Licensing page. Clicking it exports a small `.txt` file
containing your system_id, hardware fingerprint, currently-running
version, and (when a license is already installed) your customer
contact + current tier/cap/SUP context.

Send that file to your vendor by whatever channel you have available
— email from a connected workstation, USB transfer, etc. Your vendor
will return a license `.txt` you install on the same page using the
existing drag-and-drop install card.

The download works whether or not you already have a license
installed; brand-new deployments can use it to request their first
license without typing anything.

## What's unchanged

- License installation (drop the vendor's `.txt` on the Licensing
  page) is unchanged. Existing licenses continue to work.
- All other workflows — camera enrollment, alerts, reports, backups,
  software updates — are unchanged.

## For air-gap deployments

If you're already on this release stream, the Updates page **Install
from file** card will recognise this `.adcupdate` once you carry it
in. Drop the bundle, review the notes, and install — the same flow
as v0.1.29.

## Closes out

- Carry-forward item #2 from the v0.1.27 plan ("offline activation
  polish") shipped end-to-end.

## v0.1.29 — `compose/scripts/` now ships in the air-gap bundle

### What this fixes

v0.1.27 added a way to ship the **top-level** host-side scripts
(`backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `update.sh`, `install.sh`, etc.) inside the
`.adcupdate` bundle. v0.1.28 fixed a critical air-gap install bug by
adding a `--packages-json` flag to `record-versions.sh` — but
`record-versions.sh` lives in `compose/scripts/`, a sibling directory the
bundle wasn't touching. So customers who installed v0.1.28 still had the
old `record-versions.sh` on disk and had to manually copy the new one in.

v0.1.29 extends the bundle to ship `compose/scripts/` too, with its own
whitelist of customer-runtime helpers (`record-versions.sh`,
`first-run.sh`, `generate-mqtt-certs.sh`, `generate-ssl.sh`, and the
`adc-*` shortcuts). Vendor-side build tooling that lives in the same
directory (`build-adcupdate-bundle.sh`, `build-packages-json.py`,
`sign-update-manifest.sh`) is deliberately excluded — those run only in
the release CI and have no business on a customer's host.

### Why it matters

From v0.1.29 onwards, any future fix to `record-versions.sh` or other
compose-side helpers will reach customers through the normal
**Install from file** path — no `scp` required, no out-of-band steps.
Previous copies are snapshotted to `compose/scripts/.previous-<timestamp>/`
so a regression can be rolled back by `cp -r`.

### Internal note

This is the symmetric counterpart to the existing `scripts/.previous-*`
snapshot behavior that v0.1.27 introduced. Both apply paths now use a
shared helper function instead of duplicated inline logic, so future
script-shipping additions only need a whitelist entry.

### Upgrade

Standard install through the Updates page → **Install from file** with
the v0.1.29 `.adcupdate`. No data changes, no schema migrations.

## v0.1.28 — air-gap install correctness fix

### What this fixes

Customers who installed v0.1.27 via the air-gap **Install from file** path
saw the Updates page continue to show **"1 update available · v0.1.27"**
even after a successful install. Two root causes:

- **The MQTT ingest worker wasn't actually getting updated.** The catalog
  used the service name `mqtt-ingest` while the rest of the stack (Docker
  Compose, the api's target selector) calls it `ingest-worker`. The
  install-target diff joins by service name and silently skipped it. The
  fix renames the catalog entry to match.
- **Some images record an "image-id" digest after offline load** rather
  than the registry manifest digest. The Updates page compared the
  recorded digest against the catalog's manifest digest, found a
  mismatch, and reported an update as still pending. Fixed by having
  the post-install version recorder trust the just-installed bundle's
  catalog digest when the local image record is missing the registry
  origin info.

### Who should install this

Anyone who installed v0.1.27. Symptom is purely cosmetic — the rest of
the stack is healthy — but the false-positive warning is annoying.

### Upgrade path

Standard install through the Updates page. Use the same **Install from
file** card you used for v0.1.27. After install completes, the warning
will clear and the Updates page will read "Up to date · v0.1.28".

## v0.1.27 — Vendor portal Phase 2, automatic script updates, license UX polish

### Highlights

**Air-gap script updates** — Installing this release also updates the host-side
helper scripts (`backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `update.sh`, etc.). Previously these
only changed via manual file copy, which doesn't work on air-gap deployments.
Your previous copies are snapshotted under `scripts/.previous-<timestamp>/` if
you ever need to roll back.

**License page** — Removed licenses now hide by default. A footer shows
`N removed licenses hidden — auto-purge after 24h — [Show] [Purge now]`.
The auto-purge sweep runs hourly in the background; Purge-now triggers it
immediately via the new `POST /system/licenses/purge_removed` endpoint.

**Disaster recovery hardening**
- `backup.sh` no longer fails on fresh installs that have no alert snapshots
  yet (the alert-archive step now gracefully skips an empty volume rather
  than erroring out)
- `restore.sh` smoke probe now correctly recognizes a healthy stack — was
  treating the auth-required `/api/v1/health` 401 as a failure and
  false-reporting a successful restore as broken

**Vendor portal** (for the AIDataCollect operator, not customers)
- New Systems inspector pages: `/systems` and `/systems/{id}` show every
  license issued for a given customer install, with revoked rows dimmed
- Per-row Revoke action on the system detail page (vendor-ledger-only;
  customer-side enforcement ships with CRL in a future release)
- Sign form pre-fills `system_id` from URL query parameter, enabling
  one-click "issue another license for this system" deep-links
- `device_cap` default lowered from 50 → 5 to make accidental wide-open
  licenses less likely

### Upgrade notes

Standard install through the Updates page. The new script-shipping behavior
takes effect on this install — meaning your existing `backup.sh`/`restore.sh`
will be replaced with the v0.1.27 versions, with the old copies preserved
under `scripts/.previous-<timestamp>/`.

## v0.1.25 — audit-trail completeness for camera lifecycle

### Camera lifecycle now writes audit rows at every transition

The audit log was missing two of the four lifecycle events and
mis-attributing a third:

- **Enrollment** (`POST /api/v1/devices/`) wrote `cameras` and
  `camera_credentials` rows but no audit row, so compliance reviews
  had to infer "who enrolled this camera" from the `cameras` row's
  `registered_at` alone — with no operator attribution.
- **Restore from trash** wrote an audit row, but hardcoded
  `actor_username="system"` even though restore is an operator
  action gated by `manage_devices` permission. A malicious or
  accidental restore looked like a background event.
- **24-hour auto-purge sweep** (`HealthService._purge_trashed_cameras`)
  silently hard-DELETEd rows once the restore window expired, so
  the audit trail terminated at `camera_deleted` and never recorded
  the row leaving the table.

v0.1.25 fixes all three. The camera lifecycle now reads cleanly
end-to-end in the audit log:

| Stage | Action | Actor |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Wizard enroll | `camera_registered` (new) | operator |
| Portal soft-delete | `camera_deleted` | operator |
| Portal restore | `camera_restored` | operator (was "system") |
| 24h+ auto-purge | `camera_auto_purged` (new) | system (correctly — no operator) |

Detail JSON on each row carries the relevant context — `friendly_name`,
`ip_address`, `manufacturer`, `model`, the symmetric teardown summary
on delete, the re-enable summary on restore, the `trashed_at` delta
on auto-purge. Sufficient for compliance review without joining other
tables.

### First-run.sh: clean up `/var/lib/aidatacollect/{backups,snapshots}` ownership

Cosmetic follow-on to the v0.1.23 Bug E parent-dir chown. The
`backups` and `snapshots` subdirectories used to land as root:root
0777 because docker auto-creates bind-mount targets with that
default. Worked because 0777 made them world-writable, but the
ownership mismatch was ugly and the same trap-class that bit
SFTPGo home_dir (Bug B) and the api state dir (Bug E). first-run.sh
now pre-creates both subdirs with 1001:1001 and 0755, matching the
parent. Fresh-install only — existing installs are unaffected (and
already work because of the 0777 mode that's still in place there).

### Upgrade notes

- Image swap only — no schema migrations, no manual steps.
- New audit actions show up immediately on the first enroll / restore
  / purge after the update. Existing audit rows are unchanged.
- The first-run.sh chown change runs only on fresh installs; existing
  deployments do not need to do anything.
- No customer-visible behavior change beyond richer audit trails.

## v0.1.24 — heatmap cleanup fix

### adc-api can finally delete aged heatmap PNGs

The heatmap_purge cycle has been logging this on every retention
pass since heatmaps were introduced:

```
WARNING api.services.heatmap_purge Failed to delete \
  /data/heatmaps/<sha>.png: PermissionError
```

Cosmetic warning but a real slow leak — `/data/heatmaps/` grows
without bound because adc-api (uid 1001) can't unlink files in a
root-owned directory. Same root-owned-volume family as the
SFTPGo and api-state-dir fixes in v0.1.22 / v0.1.23.

`adc-sftpingest` now chowns `/data/heatmaps/` to uid 1001 at
startup, so the api side has the directory write+exec it needs
to remove files past retention. Idempotent — heals on update
without any operator action.

### Upgrade notes

- Image swap only — no schema migrations, no manual steps.
- The chown fires on the first adc-sftpingest startup after the
  update. From that point, retention deletes work cleanly and the
  WARNINGs stop.
- Existing root-owned PNGs get chowned along with the parent
  directory, so the next purge cycle catches up on the backlog.
- No customer-visible behavior change beyond the slow `/data/heatmaps/`
  growth stopping.

## v0.1.23 — quality + reliability pass

### Camera enrollment is more forgiving

Hanwha cameras occasionally wedged during enrollment when the
configure step fired its ~30 SUNAPI calls back-to-back (the camera's
web UI also stopped responding for a minute or two). The cdp_v2
client now paces requests with a small inter-call delay and
auto-retries once on transient network errors. End result: enrollments
that previously needed two attempts now usually succeed first time.

### "Backup before update" now works for app-only updates

Pre-v0.1.23 the toggle was only shown when a stateful service
(TimescaleDB / EMQX / Redis / SFTPGo) was in the diff. App-only
updates silently skipped the backup even with the box ticked. Now the
checkbox is shown for any installable update, and ticking it runs
`backup.sh` synchronously before the first image pull — useful when
a release ships a schema migration that needs a clean rollback path.

### No more PermissionError WARNINGs at adc-api startup

Fresh installs were writing this on first boot:

```
WARNING api.services.system_updates: could not persist manifest: PermissionError
WARNING api.services.network_mode: sidecar write failed (PermissionError); skipping
```

The api process falls back to in-memory state when its sidecar files
can't be written, so the warnings were cosmetic — but they meant the
Updates page and Closed-Network heuristic both lost their state across
api restarts. `first-run.sh` now pre-creates
`/var/lib/aidatacollect/` with the right ownership before the api
container starts.

### Driver Packs admin page removed

The page (Settings → Driver Packs) had been decorative since the
cdp_v2 facelift — uploading .cdp files no longer affected enrollment.
The page and its admin endpoints are removed; the service endpoints
that the ingest worker depends on stay in place. No customer action
needed.

### Under the hood

- ~1000 lines of dead post-cdp_v2-facelift code removed across api +
  portal.
- Migration audit verified the v0.1.6→v0.1.22 hop is schema-clean —
  api `_run_migrations()` was not touched in that range.

### Upgrade notes

- Image swap only — no schema migrations, no manual steps.
- Cameras already enrolled keep working as-is. Re-enrollment is not
  required.
- If you've been ignoring PermissionError WARNINGs in adc-api logs,
  they'll go away after this update.

# v0.1.22

Hotfix release. If you ran into "MQTT not connected" or "SFTP test failed" on the last step of the camera enrollment wizard — especially on a fresh install or after a factory reset — this is the release you want.

## What's fixed

### Camera enrollment now actually completes on first attempt

Three install-path bugs that turned a clean install into a multi-step manual recovery on v0.1.21:

- **SFTP "permission denied"** — `first-run.sh` provisioned the SFTPGo `camera` user (added in v0.1.21) but the home directory was created by a sibling service running as root, so SFTPGo itself couldn't write files into it. Install-time chown is now wired in; camera report uploads land on the first try.
- **MQTT silent TLS failure on re-installs** — the camera trust store check was matching certs by name only. Customers re-installing the stack onto an existing camera (which still had the prior install's CA cert) silently kept the old cert and TLS handshake failed against the new broker. Now the install computes a thumbprint and replaces a stale CA cleanly when names collide.
- **Inline-entered camera credentials weren't being saved** — operators who typed `admin` / password into the wizard rather than picking a stored credential ended up with a camera row in the DB that had no credential link. The wizard's MQTT/SFTP disable on delete then silently skipped because there were no credentials to authenticate to the camera with. Credentials entered inline are now persisted automatically.

### Camera-side cleanup when you remove a camera from the portal

Removing a camera from the portal now does a proper symmetric teardown on the camera itself:

1. Disables the camera's MQTT client (stops it talking to the broker)
2. Disables the four daily SFTP report uploads
3. Re-binds the MQTT TLS cert reference to the camera's default root cert
4. Removes our `AIDataCollect` CA from the camera's trust store

This keeps the camera in a clean state so a future re-enrollment — or a different stack install enrolling the same physical camera — doesn't trip the cert-name collision bug above.

If you Restore-within-24h, the symmetric restore step re-pushes the CA and re-binds MQTT, so a restored camera resumes traffic without any extra steps.

## Upgrading
- **Connected sites** — Settings → System → Updates → Install all.
- **Closed-network sites** — download the `.adcupdate` bundle below and use Install from file.

If you're freshly installing from scratch (not upgrading), grab the latest `install.sh` from the deploy repo and run it. The SFTPGo and chown fixes only ship via `first-run.sh`, so a fresh install picks them up automatically.

# v0.1.21

## What's new

### Camera enrollment reliability (the big one)
Two longstanding bugs were causing the wizard to show **MQTT — not connected** and **SFTP — test failed** even when the camera was actually delivering data fine. Both are fixed:

- **MQTT status badge** now reads the camera's actual connection state. Previously the parser was looking at the wrong field name and silently treating every camera as "configured but not connected" regardless of what the camera reported. Wizards on newer Hanwha firmware (W9 family, e.g. XNV-A9084R) will now flip to a green dot the moment the camera connects.
- **SFTP probe poll window** was too tight (10s ceiling) and would call a slower camera as "not connected" even when the report upload was about to succeed a second later. Bumped to 18s so a slower-network camera still gets caught.

If you previously saw yellow/red dots on the last wizard step that didn't match reality, re-enroll the affected camera after upgrading and the badges should match what the camera is actually doing.

### Reports delivery now works on fresh installs
On a brand-new install, the SFTP server's user table was empty, so the first time a camera tried to deliver a report it would silently fail with "user not found." Reports would never arrive and nothing in the UI explained why. `first-run.sh` now provisions the camera user during install. Re-running `first-run.sh` is idempotent — it'll refresh the password rather than error out.

This affects new installs only. Existing sites where reports are already flowing are unaffected.

### Licensing
- **Identity_unreadable band** — when the license server can't read the host's stable identity (a transient OS issue, mid-update, etc.), the system now surfaces that explicitly in the License page instead of falling back to a generic "verification failed" message. Operators can tell at a glance whether the issue is the license itself or a host-side identity readback.
- **Capacity check fails closed** on a DB error. Previously a transient query failure would let enrollment slip through. Now it errs on the safe side and refuses enrollment until the DB is reachable again.
- **"Signed by" label** in the License page is now clearer that it refers to the advisory envelope, not the verified key — a small but important distinction when troubleshooting a license that's correctly signed but not yet trusted.
- **Fingerprint computed at most once per minute** under heavy reverify load — eliminates redundant kernel reads during every-tick license checks.

## Upgrading
- **Connected sites** — Settings → System → Updates → Install all.
- **Closed-network sites** — download the `.adcupdate` bundle below and use Install from file.

Coming from v0.1.18 or earlier? Upgrade goes straight to v0.1.21 — no intermediate hops needed.

# v0.1.20

## What's new

### Closed Network First
For sites running on a closed network (no outbound internet), the system now detects that automatically and adapts the Updates page so it doesn't spam you with "couldn't reach the update server" errors. You'll see a dedicated **Closed Network** banner with a clear path to install updates from a `.adcupdate` file.

- **Auto-detection** — after 3 consecutive network errors fetching the update catalog, the system flips to closed-network mode. It flips back automatically once the catalog is reachable again.
- **Operator pin** — if you want to lock the mode regardless of network conditions (for demo, air-gap, or a transient outage), the new pin row on the Updates page lets you set Auto / Connected / Closed explicitly.
- **Closed-network hero** shows your running version and a button to install from file.

### Updates page polish
A round of cleanup based on running it day-to-day:

- **Install from file** is now its own card near the top, so it's easy to find whether or not you're on a closed network.
- The up-to-date hero now reads "**You're on the latest version · vX.Y.Z**" — affirmative and clear.
- A new **Release notes** button on both connected and closed-network heroes jumps you to the full notes for the next release, even when an update is already pending.
- The **Install all** confirm modal now shows the full release notes (not just a snippet), so you can review what's changing before clicking Install.
- "Specific build (hotfix)" — the password-gated path for vendor-issued hotfixes — has been simplified to a single-column layout.

## Upgrading
- **Connected sites** — visit Settings → System → Updates, click "Install all".
- **Closed-network sites** — download the `.adcupdate` bundle from the release asset below and upload it via Install from file on the Updates page.

If you're currently running v0.1.18 or older, the upgrade path goes through v0.1.20 directly — no intermediate hops required.

## What's in v0.1.19

This is a polish release that closes the four follow-ups from the
v0.1.18 lab pass. No schema changes, no migrations — image swap only.

### Bug fixes

- **Rollback now keeps state files in sync.** After clicking "Roll back
  last update", the recorded version (shown in the sidebar and on the
  Updates page) used to keep claiming the *post-update* version even
  though the *pre-update* images were restored. The portal will now
  report the version that's actually running.

- **Air-gap install progress no longer overshoots.** During an install
  from a `.adcupdate` bundle, the progress counter occasionally flashed
  a higher current value than total (e.g. "8 / 4") for one tick before
  settling. The counter now tracks the number of image tars in the
  bundle for the load phase, and the per-updated-service count for the
  pull / recreate phases.

### UX polish

- **Sidebar "update available" chip auto-clears after install.** When
  an install reaches Complete, the chip and Dashboard tile now refresh
  themselves within a few seconds — no more manual Refresh click on
  the Updates page just to clear a stale notification.

- **Upload-progress line clears when the confirm modal opens.** After
  uploading a `.adcupdate` file, the "Uploading … 100%" status line
  used to linger behind the install-confirmation dialog. It now goes
  away as soon as the upload finishes, leaving a clean confirm view.

### Upgrade notes

- Existing installs running v0.1.18 (or earlier) can upgrade in place
  via the Updates page.
- No backup is required: this release does not touch stateful services
  (database, MQTT broker, Redis, SFTP). The standard image swap is
  reversible via the "Roll back last update" button if needed.

# v0.1.15 — Cosmetic hotfix: drop duplicate "v" prefix on Updates page

Tiny hotfix for a UI typo. The Selected release card title and several install confirm dialogs on System → Updates were rendering `vv0.1.13` (two `v`s) because the version string already includes the `v` prefix from the catalog. v0.1.15 strips the duplicate.

## Affected text

- Selected release card title (`Selected release · v0.1.15`)
- Install confirm modal title (`Install v0.1.15?` / `Install v0.1.15 from file?`)
- "What's in v0.1.15" details panel inside the install confirm
- Hotfix / air-gap / catalog install success messages
- Downloaded release-notes filename (`aidatacollect-v0.1.15-release-notes.txt`)

No backend changes — portal-only.

## What's new

- **Updates page reshuffle.** The Selected release card with its release notes is now the first thing you see, right under the catalog status hero. Less scrolling to find "what would I be installing if I click Install all?"

- **Beta channel folded into Selected release.** The standalone Release channel card is gone — beta is now a small inline toggle at the bottom of the Selected release card ("Channel: [beta + release / release only]"). Same functionality, less screen real estate.

- **Per-service digest table collapsed by default.** The Installed images table is now hidden behind a "Show per-service digest details" expander. Most operators don't need to see digests during a normal upgrade; expanding stays one click away for debugging and support cases.

- **Release notes preview in the install confirm dialog.** When you click **Install all**, the confirmation now shows a "What's in vX.Y.Z" snippet of the release notes inside the dialog itself — so you can't accidentally install something without seeing at least the headline of what's changing. Full notes remain visible on the page above.

- **Softer empty-state copy.** Per-service rows where the catalog has no matching entry (typically a known naming difference like `ingest-worker` vs `mqtt-ingest`) now render as `—` with a tooltip instead of an alarming "NO REMOTE INFO" label.

## Upgrade notes

No configuration changes. Purely a UI refresh — install/rollback/restore logic is unchanged from v0.1.12.

New `releaseNotesSnippet()` plain-text helper feeds the Install confirm modal's `details` slot with the first paragraph of `release_notes_md`. ## What's new

- **Smoother install confirmation dialogs.** When you click **Install all**, **Roll back**, or other update actions, the confirmation now appears as a styled dialog that matches the rest of the portal instead of the browser's default popup. This works the same regardless of your browser's dialog settings, and looks better in dark mode and on mobile.

- **Clearer per-action wording.** Each dialog now distinguishes between safe operations (regular install with backup) and riskier ones (skipping backup on stateful services, installing prerelease hotfixes) with color-coded buttons and an icon — warning amber for normal installs, danger red for actions that bypass safety nets.

- **Keyboard-friendly.** Press **Esc** to cancel or **Enter** to confirm — same as before, just on a properly themed dialog.

No configuration changes. The change is purely how the confirmation dialogs render — the underlying install/rollback/restore logic is unchanged from v0.1.11.

## Catastrophic fixes (v10.16-A class)

v0.1.6 closes two errors that v0.1.5 lab verification surfaced post-wizard.

**api `0c06fe7` develop**:
- **#22** alerts.py:ensure_tables() ran CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX / ALTER TABLE on every /alerts/* request with zero locking. When the portal swapped to the dashboard right after wizard finalize, concurrent /alerts/?... and /alerts/hourly?... requests raced on pg_class_relname_nsp_index → transient 500s. Same class of race v0.1.3 closed for main schema-init via pg_advisory_xact_lock. Hoisted alerts DDL into _run_migrations; alerts.py:ensure_tables stays as idempotent defense-in-depth.
- **#23** cdp_v2_reprobe selected c.device_model — column was never defined in any schema. The error was masked pre-v0.1.5 by the camera_credentials UndefinedTableError on the same JOIN; v0.1.5 closed the table error, exposing this dead column reference. Dropped from query.

Other repos: no-op tag bumps. Recommended for every v0.1.5 install.

v0.1.3 closes the v0.1.2 transient race window.

v0.1.2 used `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` + early return for the migration loser worker, but that loser then started its background services BEFORE the winner's migration transaction committed — producing a ~5s window of transient `UndefinedTable` errors in service logs + a single HTTP 500 on the first dashboard load.

**Fix (api `d330fbf` develop)**: switch to blocking `pg_advisory_xact_lock`. Loser waits for winner's COMMIT (which releases the xact-lock) before proceeding. By the time it starts services, schema is committed and visible. No more transient first-tick window.

Other repos in this release are no-op tag bumps. Recommended for any v0.1.2 fresh install that observed transient errors at boot. Same compatibility envelope as v0.1.2 (`from: v0.1.0`).

v0.1.2 hotfix release. Critical schema-init race fix plus 4 other install-path bugs caught in v0.1.1 lab smoke.

**Fixes:**
- **(#16, CRITICAL)** `aidatacollect-api`: schema-init race. Two uvicorn workers concurrently called `create_hypertable`, colliding on `pg_type_typname_nsp_index` and leaving the schema half-applied (missing tables: sites, zone_display_names; missing column: mqtt_transport). Fix: serialize `_run_migrations` with `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` + eager base-table creates + per-statement SAVEPOINTs.
- **(#17)** install-history.json chmod 0644 → 0666 so the api container can write the trial anti-cheat anchor on /setup/finalize.
- **(#13)** first-run.sh writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-aidatacollect-reserved-ports.conf reserving SFTPGo passive 60000-60010 from the kernel ephemeral pool (32768-60999) so `docker compose up` never races a transient ephemeral source port.
- **(#14)** install.sh + first-run.sh recovery panels print copy-pastable absolute paths + remind about `newgrp docker`.
- **(#15)** first-run.sh auto re-execs under `sg docker -c` when the user is in the docker group but the shell session predates the group add.
